summary: Takezo Kaneko was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1926–1929). He held posts at Hokkaido University (~1940–1944), the University of Tokyo (professor, ~1947–1966), International Christian University (~1966–1976), and Seikei University (~1976–1980).

Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé, succeeded Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö in 2012, and taught Phakchok Rinpoche.

Takudo Ishikawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held appointments as a researcher at the Research Institute of Jodo Shu (attested 2005) and as a specially appointed full-time lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2015).

Takushu Sugimoto works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Tohoku University, studying under Ensho Kanakura, Hakuyu Hadano, and others, later supervised by Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha. He taught at Kanazawa, Komazawa, and Kinjo Universities.

Buddhist studies scholar Tampalawela Dhammaratana studied at Kelaniya, the University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études with Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

Tan Chung specializes in history, archaeology, and Sinology, earning a PhD from Visva-Bharati University. He held positions at the National Defence Academy, University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, the Institute of Chinese Studies, and Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Tan Poh Beng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015) under supervisors Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam, also studying under Sumanasiri and Shengshou.
Tan Sitong was a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Wang Zhengyi as well as Yang Renshan (~1896–1897).

Tan Yun-shan was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. After studying at institutions including Hunan First Normal University and under Taixu, he co-founded Visva-Bharati University, serving as Professor of Chinese Studies there (~1937–1968).
Tanero Sasakawa worked in Sinology, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896) and later held posts at Toyo University and Meiji University.

Tansen Sen specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Peking University under Yinzeng Geng and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, later holding a post at Baruch College (attested 2003).
Tanso Hirose was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kamei Juku (~1797–1801) and under Hodo, later founding Kangien in 1801.

Tanzan Hara worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at Shoheizaka Gakumonjo and under traditional teachers. He held posts at the Ministry of Religion, University of Tokyo, Japan Academy, and Komazawa University, and founded Bussensha.

Tanzan Ishibashi was a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University (~1903–1907). He held positions at Yokohama Mainichi Shimbun, Toyo Keizai, and served as president of Rissho University (~1952–1968).

Tao Jiang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo and was an associate professor of religion at Rutgers University (attested 2011).
Tao Jin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD in 2008 from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under the supervision of Alexander L. Mayer.
Tao Pan is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned a BA from Fudan University in 2010 and a Magister Artium from the University of Munich.
Tarab Tulku worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Copenhagen and served as a curator at the Royal Danish Library (~1967–2000).

Tarthang Tulku works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968), and founded the Nyingma Institute, Dharma Publishing, and Dharma College.

Taryo Makita was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University (~1936–1939). He held faculty posts at Kyoto University, Gifu University of Education, and Saitama Institute of Technology, where he served as president.
